Like said a wise man :

The second big thing to consider when making a humanoid SCP object is avoiding "X-men Syndrome". As a rule of thumb, if what's anomalous about your humanoid SCP object can be most accurately described as a voluntary "power" or "ability", you should probably start over. Slapping on some superficially nasty drawbacks, making them ugly, and/or giving them an awful personality won't fix it, either.

The story is not bad per se (even if quite light, mostly a twist with text added around it), but SCP-638 is just not a decent SCP.

I thought this was great, but I stopped reading after encountering so many ethnic slurs.

I’m not worried about someone else being offended, I’m offended. They don’t fit with the setting (you imagine a world where gangsters of different ethnicities work together but denigrate each other).

What kind of reader do you imagine reads this and says, “This story is so much better and more realistic because you used these slurs.”

They’re not even realistic for the time you’re looking for. If you go to google books and look for these terms in books of the period, you find very little fiction using them and lot of condemnation. One book from the time recommended that children be educated about other cultures so they knew not to use these exact slurs. They concluded “Again the study of various contributions may create respect for people so hideously maligned.”

Outside of that, I would definitely upvote. The story seems great.

This came out a bit long, unfortunately, but the following is my explanation as to why I gave this article a -1.

Show
Hide

I'll start by clarifying that, when I read this page for the first time, I gave it a +1. That's because this is a good page - there's a good plot with a nice twist, all of the characters feel believable, and the setting and backstory contribute as well.

The reason I now changed my vote to a -1 is because, while I feel like this is a great contribution to the site, it's not one I feel should be in the format of an SCP article. SCPs are things the Foundation either contains or has contained, for an indefinite amount of time. This is why the articles have Containment Procedures right at the top - they're supposed to help Foundationers continue the potentially perpetual containment of the anomaly.

This article discusses a group of anomalous humans, which means the Foundation would've certainly had an interest in them, and would indeed have apprehended them as described in the article. The problem here is that, as far as I can tell, all of the events of this article take place within 2 days. The Foundation "representative" here mentions multiple times that the Foundation has no interest in indefinitely arresting these guys, and that they will be released into the regular justice system once the investigation is over.

This doesn't feel like something the Foundation would write an SCP document about. Honestly, it feels like it would've taken the Foundation a longer time to write this article than the amount of time these guys were in containment. In my opinion, this story would better fit into the world as a tale - an in-universe documentation of the investigation, perhaps. Unfortunately, this means that for now, I'm giving it a -1.
